sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface immunostaining without detergent confirmed cell-surface display of myc-tagged WT OTOA; no functional assay reported in the cited clips.
sites.rationale: OTOA is a GPI-anchored extracellular protein (topology: SP 1–22, extracellular 23–1153, no TM). The GPI anchor signal at the C-terminus is co-translationally cleaved and replaced by a GPI lipid, so any C-terminal tag would be lost. The mature N-terminus (residue 23, Y) is therefore the sole extracellular terminus that can carry a surface-displayed tag. Python verification confirms residue 22 = S (last SP residue) and residue 23 = Y (mature N-terminus); insert_after_residue = 22 places the tag immediately after SP cleavage. The position is topology-derived because the ledger clips name no specific residue. Full-length myc-tagged WT OTOA expressed in HEK293T cells; non-permeabilized (surface) immunostaining with anti-myc antibody confirmed cell-surface display (L2). OTOA is GPI-anchored with no TM segments; the C-terminal GPI signal is cleaved and replaced by the GPI lipid anchor, making the N-terminus (after SP cleavage) the sole extracellular terminus available for a tag.

sources.claim: HEK293T cells were transfected with WT OTOA and subsequently immunostained with an α-myc antibody (raised in rabbit) in the absence of a detergent for surface labeling.

literature_notes: L1 and L2 both support the same N-terminal myc-tag site on full-length WT OTOA; L2 is the stronger clip (surface display confirmed) and is used as the primary support. L3 and L4 describe a myc-tagged truncated construct (p.Gln589ArgfsX55 in paper numbering; the nearest canonical Q is at position 580) that is NOT surface-tethered because the truncation removes the GPI anchor signal — this is recorded in other_positions. No internal loop sites are supported by the ledger: the protein has no TM segments and therefore no extracellular loops in the classical sense, and no insertion experiment within any internal region of OTOA is cited. The C-terminus is not a viable surface-tag site because the GPI anchor signal is cleaved there.

literature_other_positions.note: Myc-tagged truncated OTOA (p.Gln589ArgfsX55 in paper; nearest canonical Q is at position 580) is not tethered to the cell surface; the frameshift truncation removes the GPI anchor signal, abolishing surface display.
